priorStories.headline: World court finds Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
priorStories.body:
The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during military operations in northern Rakhine State in 2017. It also found that Myanmar failed to prevent and punish genocide.

The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those responsible, facilitate safe and voluntary returns, restore property and provide compensation. The judgment determines Myanmar’s responsibility as a state; it does not convict individuals of crimes.

sources.name: International Court of Justice — press release hosted by UNHCR Refworld
UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar

candidates.summary: The Office for National Statistics released October retail figures showing that sales volumes in Great Britain rose 0.7% from September and 2.3% from a year earlier. Volumes increased 0.4% over the three months to October compared with the preceding three months. Supermarkets reported increased purchases of long-life food following the government's Be Ready campaign; clothing sales also strengthened.
candidates.title: Great Britain retail sales rose 0.7% in October, official figures show

candidates.summary: Taiwan's Taiex closed Friday down 6.2% at 36,033.29, bringing its weekly decline to 17.5%. South Korea's Kospi closed down 5.2% at 4,869.96, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 5.1% to 56,436.65. Technology and semiconductor shares were among the largest decliners.
candidates.title: Taiwan, South Korea and Japan stock indexes close sharply lower

candidates.summary: Polish officials said three Russian objects, believed to be two missiles and a jet-powered drone, entered Polish airspace and came down in southeastern Poland on November 20. Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as an apparent intentional provocation coinciding with European military exercises for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. The identification of all three objects remained preliminary.
candidates.title: Poland reports Russian airspace violations during European military exercises

candidates.summary: Estonia's government decided on November 20 to close road border crossings with Russia from December 1, citing Russian hostile activities. The suspension is planned for at least six months, after which the government will decide whether to extend it. Russia's Foreign Ministry criticized the decision and threatened political and diplomatic responses. The crossings had not closed under this decision at the time of reporting.
candidates.title: Estonia decides to close road border crossings with Russia from December 1

candidates.summary: Iraqi security forces established a command headquarters on the outskirts of Jurf al-Sakhar on November 20, entering a longtime stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia. Two Iraqi officials told AP that an agreement allowed security forces to enter without an immediate militia withdrawal. The deployment included army, federal police, energy-sector police and Popular Mobilization Forces personnel; the agreement envisaged Kataib Hezbollah withdrawing within a month.
candidates.title: Iraqi forces establish headquarters near Kataib Hezbollah stronghold

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema ruled from the bench on November 20 to block construction of President Trump's proposed 250-foot memorial arch while Arlington County's lawsuit proceeds, according to plaintiffs' lawyers. The injunction has no specified expiration date. It is separate from a Washington federal court's temporary restraining order, extended on November 18 through December 3.
candidates.title: Second federal judge blocks construction of Trump's proposed memorial arch

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed sharply lower on November 20. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, the Nasdaq composite dropped 5.3% to 22,617.73, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.9% to 48,147.33. The S&P 500 finished more than 10% below its October 6 record and lost 8.6% for the week. The Nasdaq turned negative for the year.
candidates.title: S&P 500 closes in correction as Nasdaq falls 5.3%

candidates.summary: At a November 20 White House news conference, President Trump threatened a large tax on U.S. companies that build artificial intelligence data centers abroad. He said he had not yet told his staff about the proposal. No tax rate, enforcement mechanism or implementation timetable was provided; the remarks did not establish an enacted tax or prohibition.
candidates.title: Trump proposes tax penalties for U.S. companies building AI data centers abroad

candidates.summary: COP31 negotiations in Antalya continued beyond their scheduled November 20 finish without agreement. Fossil fuels and climate finance remained disputed. The latest draft political decision, published November 19, omitted fossil fuels and did not reiterate the earlier commitment to transition away from them. That text remained a negotiating draft, not an adopted agreement.
candidates.title: COP31 talks run into overtime with fossil fuels and financing unresolved

candidates.summary: President Trump said at his November 20 White House news conference that Iran wanted an agreement to end hostilities but had not offered terms acceptable to him. AP also reported, citing an unnamed Middle Eastern diplomat, that Gulf Arab states were using existing communications channels to seek a partial solution involving shipping access through the Strait of Hormuz and limited sanctions relief. No agreement was announced.
candidates.title: Trump says Iran's proposed terms remain unacceptable as Gulf mediation continues

candidates.summary: A federal jury on November 20 convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce, following a retrial after his first trial ended in a mistrial. Prosecutors established that the January 1, 2025 Lachman Fire continued smoldering underground before resurfacing on January 7 as the Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. Sentencing remains pending.
candidates.title: Federal jury convicts Jonathan Rinderknecht in Palisades Fire retrial

sources.name: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California

candidates.summary: An earthquake struck central Peru at 00:09 UTC on November 21, equivalent to 7:09 p.m. November 20 in Peru and New York. GDACS listed its magnitude as 6.7. Reuters reported that shaking prompted residents in Lima to leave their homes and lawmakers to evacuate Congress. There were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage. The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat.
candidates.title: Earthquake strikes central Peru and is felt in Lima

sources.name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
